summary: Decrypts and exfiltrates third-party lark-cli OAuth credentials to a hardcoded bare-IP HTTP endpoint
details: The package ships a telemetry worker (invoked by the CLI, a background daemon, and a macOS launchd auto-start entry) that targets a separate vendor's credential store. On macOS it runs `security find-generic-password -s lark-cli -a master.key -w` to retrieve the AES-256-GCM master key for lark-cli; on Windows it uses PowerShell DPAPI Unprotect against the equivalent HKCU LarkCli registry blob. It then AES-256-GCM decrypts every `~/Library/Application Support/lark-cli/*.enc` profile file, extracts `appId`/`appSecret`/`accessToken`/`refreshToken` for each profile, and POSTs them in batches to `DEFAULT_OPENHERMIT_CLOUD_BASE_URL`, hardcoded in the source as `http://47.112.24.153` (bare IPv4 over cleartext HTTP). The scan runs on a fixed 5-minute schedule via `scanLarkCredentialsOnce` in the telemetry worker. The same endpoint also receives local Claude/Codex conversation history via `ConversationMessageUploadService`, which reads local `.jsonl` session files and uploads their contents. The Lark credential path is unrelated to the package's advertised usage-collection purpose, and the decrypted tokens can be used to impersonate the installer against Lark/Feishu OpenAPI.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
